# graph-manager: floating spec pane on the Terminals page (auto-open + chip)

## What to build

On the Terminals page, watch the specs of the focused pane's workspace and show the one being written in a floating pane over the terminals. Already in the codebase:
- **Server:** `GET /api/workspaces/:id/specs` → `{ specs: [{ path, name, title, mtimeMs, size }] }` (newest first, `docs/prd/*.md` only) and `GET /api/workspaces/:id/specs/file?path=docs/prd/x.md` → `{ path, text, mtimeMs }` (404 when gone) in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/specs.ts`.
- **Web:** `<SpecView text theme />` in `apps/graph-manager/src/web/components/SpecView.tsx`, which renders Markdown and Mermaid safely.

The pane opens by itself when a spec in that workspace gets a newer `mtimeMs` than any seen since the page loaded, and follows it while it is written. It can be dragged, resized and closed. A `spec <name>` chip on the terminal's pane head reopens it. The user reads the spec there and answers the agent in the terminal; there is no approve button.

Spec: `docs/prd/graph-manager-spec-view.md` (section "Web: floating spec pane on the Terminals page", user stories 1-3).

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx`:
  - lines 73-135 — the page component, `useOverview()`, layout state and `focusedItem = state.panes[state.focused]` (line 134);
  - lines 334-357 — `renderPane`: a terminal pane gets `term`, `liveRun`, …; `parseItem(item)` gives `{ kind: "term", id }` or `{ kind: "run", ws, runId }`. The focused workspace is `byId.get(p.id)?.workspaceId` for a terminal, or `p.ws` for a run; the same logic is at lines 483-489 (`defaultWorkspace`);
  - lines 386-475 — `<main className="terms-main">` with the tab bar and `.terms-grid`; the floating pane renders inside `<main>` after the grid (it needs `position: relative` on `.terms-main` or use `position: fixed`);
  - lines 42-58 — `useNarrow()` (under 900 px).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/TerminalPane.tsx` (lines 16-45 `PaneChrome`/`PaneHead`, lines 47-130 `TerminalPane`) — add the spec chip in `PaneHead`'s `extra` next to the run chip; mirror the run chip markup: `<button type="button" className="run-chip run-chip-head" …>`; lines 155-180 `RunPane` — the polling pattern with `api<…>()` + `window.setInterval(…, POLL_MS)` and cleanup.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/overview.tsx` (lines 100-125) — polling that pauses while `document.visibilityState === "hidden"`; mirror it in the specs hook.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/api.ts` — `api<T>(path)` (throws `ApiError` with `status`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/runs.ts` line 88 — `POLL_MS = 2000`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/layout.ts` (lines 1-5, 150-170) — how layout is saved in `localStorage` with a safe accessor; do the same for `gm.specPane` (`{ x, y, w, h }`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/theme.ts` — `useTheme().resolved` for `SpecView`'s `theme`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/Icon.tsx` — available icon names (use `close`, `maximize` or whatever exists; do not add new SVGs unless needed).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.css` (lines 33-40 `.run-chip`, 46, 69, 78-95 `.tp-head`) — styles to mirror; tokens in `ui/tokens.css`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.test.tsx` (lines 1-120) — the page test harness: `vi.mock("../components/TerminalView", …)`, a `fetch` stub routing `/api/...` URLs to JSON (`json(status, body)`), `OverviewProvider`, `ToastProvider`, `MemoryRouter`, fake data `WORKSPACES`, `TERMS`, `RUNS`. Extend this harness; mock `../components/SpecView` with a stand-in that prints its `text` so tests do not need marked/mermaid.

## Patterns to follow

- Pure, unit-tested state logic in a `.ts` file (like `layout.ts` + `layout.test.ts`), UI in `.tsx`.
- `data-testid` on every element tests touch.

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/specPane.ts` (+ `specPane.test.ts`)

- **IMPLEMENT** pure helpers:
  - `export interface SpecWatch { baseline?: number; latest?: { path: string; mtimeMs: number } }`
  - `export function nextWatch(prev: SpecWatch, specs: { path: string; mtimeMs: number }[]): { watch: SpecWatch; open?: string }` — the first answer (`baseline === undefined`) sets `baseline` to the newest `mtimeMs` (0 when empty) and opens nothing. Later answers: when the newest spec's `mtimeMs > baseline`, return `open: <its path>` and raise `baseline` to it. Returns the same `open` only once per change.
  - `export interface Box { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }`, `export const DEFAULT_BOX`, `export function clampBox(b: Box, view: { w: number; h: number }): Box` (min 320×200, fully inside the view; default: right half, 44 % wide, 70 % high, 16 px margin), `loadBox()`/`saveBox()` with key `gm.specPane` and the same safe-storage accessor style as `layout.ts`.
  - Tests: baseline on first poll, open on newer mtime, no reopen for the same mtime, switching workspace resets (the caller passes a fresh `SpecWatch`), clamp cases, bad JSON in storage → default.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/SpecFloat.tsx` and `SpecFloat.css`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export function useWorkspaceSpecs(ws: string | undefined)` → `{ specs: SpecEntry[] }`, polling `/api/workspaces/${encodeURIComponent(ws)}/specs` every `POLL_MS`, paused while hidden, cleared when `ws` changes, keeping the last good answer on error.
- **IMPLEMENT** `export function SpecFloat({ ws, path, specs, narrow, onSelect, onClose })`:
  - polls `/api/workspaces/${ws}/specs/file?path=${encodeURIComponent(path)}` every `POLL_MS` while mounted; re-renders `SpecView` only when `mtimeMs` changed; keeps the scroll position of its body across updates; on 404 shows `This spec was moved or deleted.`;
  - head: drag handle (pointer events: `pointerdown` on the head, `pointermove`/`pointerup` on `window`, `setPointerCapture` when available), the spec path (`mono`), a `<select aria-label="Spec">` of `specs` (shows `name`) calling `onSelect(path)`, and a close button `aria-label="Close spec"` (`data-testid="spec-close"`);
  - a resize handle at the bottom-right corner (`aria-label="Resize spec"`), box saved with `saveBox` on pointer up, clamped with `clampBox` on window resize;
  - `Escape` while focus is inside closes it;
  - `role="dialog" aria-label="Spec <name>" aria-modal="false"`, `data-testid="spec-float"`; `narrow` → class `narrow` that fills the main area (no drag/resize);
  - `SpecView` gets `theme={useTheme().resolved}`.
- CSS: `position: absolute` inside `.terms-main` (add `position: relative` there), elevated surface, border, radius and shadow tokens, header like `.tp-head`, body `overflow: auto`, `z-index` above panes but below dialogs/toasts (check the z-index scale used in `ui/base.css` / `Drawer`).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `focusedWs` = workspace of `focusedItem` (terminal → `workspaceId`, run → `ws`), via a small helper.
  - `const { specs } = useWorkspaceSpecs(focusedWs);` a `watch` ref per workspace (reset when `focusedWs` changes) fed with `nextWatch` on every new `specs` answer; when it returns `open`, set `specOpen = { ws: focusedWs, path: open }`.
  - Render `<SpecFloat …>` inside `<main>` after the grid when `specOpen` is set and `specOpen.ws === focusedWs`; `onClose` clears `specOpen` (the watch keeps its baseline, so it reopens only on a newer change).
  - Pass to each `TerminalPane` a `spec` prop: the newest spec of that terminal's workspace — only the focused workspace is polled, so pass it for terminals of `focusedWs` only — and `onOpenSpec(path)` that sets `specOpen`.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/TerminalPane.tsx`

- **IMPLEMENT** optional props `spec?: { name: string; path: string }` and `onOpenSpec?(path: string)`; render, before the run chip, `<button type="button" className="run-chip run-chip-head spec-chip" onClick={() => onOpenSpec?.(spec.path)} data-testid="pane-spec-chip">spec {spec.name}</button>` when `spec` is set.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.test.tsx`

- **IMPLEMENT** tests with the existing harness (fake timers or `waitFor` with the real 2 s poll as the existing tests do — check which they use): (1) the specs route first returns `[{ path: "docs/prd/a.md", name: "a.md", mtimeMs: 100 }]` → no float; then `mtimeMs: 200` → `spec-float` appears with the file text (from the mocked `SpecView`); (2) close → float gone, chip `pane-spec-chip` reads `spec a.md`, click → float back; (3) same mtime again does not reopen after close; (4) a terminal without workspace → no specs request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Writing or changing `docs/prd/*.md` in the focused terminal's workspace opens the floating pane within about one poll; specs that existed at page load do not open it until they change.
- [ ] The pane updates while the file changes, can be dragged, resized (saved), closed (Escape too) and reopened from the chip.
- [ ] Narrow screens: the pane fills the main area.
- [ ] Check it in a browser yourself (TESTING.md "graph-manager" and "graph-manager UI checklist (agent-browser)"): log in, clone `octo/hello` from the fake forge, open a terminal in it, run `mkdir -p docs/prd && printf '# Demo\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  A-->B\n```\n' > docs/prd/demo.md` in that terminal, see the pane open with the diagram, screenshot and look at it; drag it, close it, reopen from the chip.
- [ ] `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/web/pages` passes.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- src/web/pages
npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager
```
